title: Antitumor Efficacy of Human Monocyte-Derived Dendritic Cells: Comparing Isolation Methods
author: Marques, Silva, et al.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs by density gradient
steps.instruction: Obtain leuko‑platelet concentrates from healthy donors, perform density‑gradient centrifugation using Biocoll, wash the recovered cells to remove platelets, split each PBMC sample for parallel processing, and conduct HLA typing to retain only HLA‑A*02:01 donors for downstream assays.

substeps.instruction: Obtain leuko‑platelet concentrates from healthy donors (IPST) with ethical approval.
Separate PBMCs by density‑gradient centrifugation using Biocoll (Biochrom).
Wash the PBMC pellet to improve platelet removal.
Divide each PBMC preparation into two equal aliquots for parallel immunomagnetic separations.
Perform HLA typing and keep only donors with an HLA‑A*02:01 profile.

steps.title: Isolate CD14+ monocytes (Miltenyi MACS)
steps.instruction: Resuspend PBMCs in PBS pH 7.2 containing 0.5 % BSA and 2 mM EDTA, label with CD14 microbeads (20 µL per 10⁷ cells) for 15 min at 4 °C, run through an LS magnetic column in a MIDIMACS separator, rinse three times, elute CD14‑negative cells, then remove the column from the magnet and elute the CD14+ fraction, wash both fractions, culture CD14+ cells and freeze CD14‑negative cells.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend PBMCs in PBS (pH 7.2) with 0.5 % BSA and 2 mM EDTA.
Add CD14 microbeads (20 µL per 10⁷ cells) and incubate 15 min at 4 °C.
Load the suspension onto an LS magnetic column placed in a MIDIMACS separator.
Rinse the column three times with the same buffer.
Collect the flow‑through (CD14‑negative cells).
Remove the column from the magnetic field and elute the retained CD14+ cells.
Wash both CD14+ and CD14‑negative fractions.
Culture the CD14+ monocytes; freeze the CD14‑negative cells for storage.

steps.title: Isolate CD14+ monocytes (EasySep)
steps.instruction: Resuspend PBMCs in PBS with 2 % FBS and 1 mM EDTA, incubate 15 min at room temperature with the Positive Selection Cocktail (TAC), add dextran‑coated EasySep magnetic nanoparticles and incubate 10 min at room temperature, place the tube in an EasySep Magnet for 5 min, invert to discard supernatant (CD14‑negative), resuspend retained CD14+ cells, repeat magnet incubation twice on the supernatant to capture any remaining CD14+ cells, then culture CD14+ cells and freeze CD14‑negative cells.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend PBMCs in PBS containing 2 % FBS and 1 mM EDTA.
Incubate 15 min at room temperature with the Positive Selection Cocktail (tetrameric antibody complexes).
Add dextran‑coated EasySep magnetic nanoparticles and incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Insert the tube into an EasySep Magnet and incubate 5 min.
Invert the tube to pour off the supernatant (CD14‑negative fraction).
Resuspend the magnetically retained CD14+ cells in buffer.
Repeat the magnet incubation twice on the discarded supernatant to capture any remaining CD14+ cells.
Harvest the CD14+ monocytes for culture; freeze the CD14‑negative cells.

steps.title: Perform flow cytometry analysis
steps.instruction: Stain cells with FITC, APC or PE‑conjugated monoclonal antibodies (anti‑CD3, anti‑CD14 from ImmunoTools; anti‑CD86 from ImmunoTools; anti‑HLA‑DR from Immunostep), acquire data on an Attune® Acoustic Focusing Cytometer using Attune® Cytometric Software v2.1, collect at least 10 000 events per gate, use FSC/SSC for size and granularity, exclude doublets via FSC‑A/FSC‑H, and calculate mean fluorescence intensity for each marker.

substeps.instruction: Prepare staining buffer and add FITC, APC, or PE‑conjugated antibodies: anti‑CD3, anti‑CD14 (ImmunoTools), anti‑CD86 (ImmunoTools), anti‑HLA‑DR (Immunostep).
Incubate cells with antibodies according to standard protocols.
Run samples on an Attune® Acoustic Focusing Cytometer.
Analyze data with Attune® Cytometric Software v2.1, acquiring ≥10 000 events in the gate of interest.
Use forward‑scatter (FSC) and side‑scatter (SSC) to assess cell size and granularity; exclude doublets based on FSC‑A vs. FSC‑H.
Determine the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) for each marker.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Ensure each experiment is performed at least three times with cells from different donors, analyze data with GraphPad Prism version 6.01, apply two‑tailed paired Student’s t test or two‑way ANOVA for multiple comparisons, present results as mean ± SEM, and consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.

substeps.instruction: Repeat each assay with cells from at least three independent donors.
Import data into GraphPad Prism v6.01.
Perform two‑tailed paired Student’s t test or two‑way ANOVA as appropriate.
Report values as mean ± standard error of the mean (SEM).
Declare differences significant when p < 0.05.
